summary: Iteration 14 v2.0 CMS architecture upgrade — verified backend + frontend. Backend pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_iter14_membership_cms.py: 24/26 PASS. Two real bugs found: (1) GET /api/membership/my-tier always returns 'free' because server.get_current_user() strips membership_tier from user dict — membership_api.get_my_tier reads user.get('membership_tier','free') on that stripped dict; DB is updated correctly (verified via /api/membership/admin/stats which reports premium:1 after PUT), but /my-tier reflects 'free'. (2) POST /api/attachments/upload silently discards the access_level Form parameter and hardcodes 'public' (attachments_api.py line 47). Embed endpoint (/api/attachments/embed) and PUT /api/attachments/{id} DO persist access_level correctly. Frontend Playwright verified: admin login works, /admin panel renders exactly 13 tabs [overview, website, chapter-notes, topics, worksheets, questions, videos, media, courses, products, users, orders, contacts] with NO 'Resources' tab; Website Content editor shows all 9 CMS page tabs [about, career-guidance, community, contact, global, home, learn, profile-building, store]; homepage still loads with 'The Premium Learning Platform for Cambridge Students' hero; /learn/igcse/physics/electricity renders with Notes/Videos/Questions/Downloads tabs; footer has 'Store' column (no /resources link); /resources no longer resolves to a Resources page (falls through catch-all to 'Board not found'). Public CMS: GET /api/cms/page/store, /learn, /community, /career-guidance, /profile-building all return hero; /api/cms/section/global/seo and /navigation return correct data. Membership: /api/membership/tiers returns 6 tiers, /access-levels returns 7 levels; admin can set tier (persists in DB, verified via stats).

critical.issue: Always returns tier='free' even after admin sets tier='premium' for the same user. RCA: server.py get_current_user() returns a dict WITHOUT membership_tier field; membership_api.py get_my_tier() reads user.get('membership_tier','free') on that dict → always defaults to 'free'. DB IS updated correctly (admin stats confirms). Fix: In membership_api.get_my_tier, load the raw user doc from db.users by _id (or add membership_tier to get_current_user return value in server.py).

access_level Form parameter is accepted but IGNORED. attachments_api.py line 47 hardcodes '"access_level": "public"'. Regardless of what the client sends (verified with access_level=premium), stored value is always 'public'. The embed endpoint AND PUT update work correctly. Fix: change line 47 to 'access_level: access_level' (use the param). Frontend TopicAttachments.js DOES send it correctly.

issues: App.js catch-all '/:board' → SubjectsList renders 'Board not found' for any unknown top-level path. /resources now shows 'Board not found' rather than a proper 404 page. Cosmetic — not blocking.
Benign 404s on /api/auth/me for anonymous visitors — carried from prior iterations.

action_items: FIX BUG (HIGH): membership_api.py get_my_tier — user dict from get_current_user does not carry membership_tier. Either (a) fetch user doc directly: `user_doc = await db.users.find_one({\"_id\": ObjectId(user['id'])}); tier_slug = user_doc.get('membership_tier','free')` OR (b) modify server.get_current_user to include membership_tier in returned dict.
FIX BUG (HIGH): attachments_api.py:47 change `\"access_level\": \"public\"` to `\"access_level\": access_level` so the Form parameter is actually persisted on /upload.
(carried) Optional: whitelist embed_url origins (YouTube/Vimeo) — still open from iter 13.
(carried) Optional: sanitize upload extensions/folder names — still open from iter 12/13.
critical_code_review_comments: cms_api.seed_cms_content: early-return at `count > 0` means the second (idempotent) new_sections block never runs on existing installs. It works right now because previous iterations had already seeded the new pages; but if someone drops db.site_content or seeds a partial subset, the idempotent branch will not fire. Recommendation: move the idempotent upsert block OUTSIDE the `if count > 0: return` guard so it always tries to add any missing new sections.

attachments_api.upload_attachment declares `access_level: str = Form('public')` but the doc payload hardcodes `\"access_level\": \"public\"` — the incoming param is unreachable (dead code). This is a copy-paste bug.

membership_api.get_my_tier depends on a field (`membership_tier`) that is not exposed by the shared get_current_user contract. Data-model / contract mismatch: either publish membership_tier from get_current_user or query the DB inside get_my_tier.

server.get_current_user returns a hand-picked subset of fields (id/email/name/role/created_at). Any downstream API that needs newer user fields (membership_tier, access_level, avatar, etc.) will silently see them as missing. Consider returning the full sanitised user doc (minus password_hash).
membership_api.set_user_tier response is bare `{message}`; consider returning the updated tier document so the caller can refresh state without a follow-up GET.
footerLinks in Footer.js hardcodes '/practice' and '/workshops' under Store column although those pages exist. Layout is fine; label 'Store' now correctly replaces 'Resources'.

App.js still has broad catch-all `/:board` → SubjectsList mounted for ANY unknown top-level path (e.g. /resources returns 'Board not found'). A dedicated NotFound component would be cleaner and prevent surprising board-lookup calls.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin tabs, CMS pages, home, learn, footer all verified)

seed_data_creation: Test creates & cleans up: 1 embed attachment + 1 uploaded 'TEST_iter14.txt' on topic_id 'TEST_iter14_topic_membership' (all deleted in teardown). Admin's membership_tier temporarily set to 'premium' during test then reverted to 'free'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 14 (v2.0 CMS architecture) — 2 real backend bugs remain: (1) /api/membership/my-tier always reports 'free' due to user-dict field-missing (server.get_current_user strips membership_tier), (2) /api/attachments/upload ignores access_level form param (hardcoded 'public' at attachments_api.py:47). Both need fixes. Regression test file: /app/backend/tests/test_iter14_membership_cms.py — the 2 known-failing tests document the exact expected fix. All 9 CMS pages seeded correctly. Admin panel has 13 tabs (no Resources). Membership tiers=6, access levels=7. Admin can set/read tiers via DB (verified via /admin/stats) — only /my-tier read path is broken.

bug1_membership_my_tier.symptom: PUT /api/membership/admin/user/{id}/tier followed by GET /api/membership/my-tier — response always shows 'free'. But GET /api/membership/admin/stats correctly shows the updated tier count (e.g. by_tier.premium=1).
bug1_membership_my_tier.reproduction: 1) POST /api/auth/login as admin. 2) me = GET /api/auth/me. 3) PUT /api/membership/admin/user/{me.id}/tier body={tier:'premium'} → 200 OK. 4) GET /api/membership/my-tier → tier.slug='free' (BUG). GET /api/membership/admin/stats → by_tier.premium=1 (DB is correct).
bug1_membership_my_tier.root_cause: server.py get_current_user() line 71-77 returns a dict with only {id,email,name,role,created_at}. It does NOT include membership_tier. membership_api.py:60 `tier_slug = user.get('membership_tier','free')` therefore ALWAYS falls back to default 'free'.
bug1_membership_my_tier.fix: In membership_api.py get_my_tier, query the DB: `user_doc = await db.users.find_one({'_id': ObjectId(user['id'])}); tier_slug = user_doc.get('membership_tier','free')`. Alternative (broader): add `membership_tier` to the fields returned by server.get_current_user() so all callers see it.

bug2_upload_access_level_hardcoded.symptom: POST /api/attachments/upload multipart with access_level=premium form field; server returns 200; but GET /api/attachments/topic/{id} shows access_level='public' for that record.
bug2_upload_access_level_hardcoded.reproduction: curl -F 'file=@x.txt' -F 'topic_id=T1' -F 'access_level=premium' -F 'attachment_type=document' /api/attachments/upload → 200. GET /api/attachments/topic/T1 → last item has access_level='public'.
bug2_upload_access_level_hardcoded.root_cause: attachments_api.py line 22 declares Form param access_level correctly. Line 47 constructs the doc with `"access_level": "public"` hardcoded — the Form param is never read.
bug2_upload_access_level_hardcoded.fix: Change line 47 from `"access_level": "public",` to `"access_level": access_level,`. One-line fix. Add a whitelist check against ACCESS_LEVELS from membership_api for defense in depth.
